summary: Fit a nonperiodic parametric spline to ordered planar boundary vertices.

identity.direction: ordered boundary vertices to an interpolable boundary object
identity.definition: Fit a SciPy parametric spline with s=0 and sample it at 200 parameters.
identity.coordinates: Vertex coordinates in caller length units.
identity.boundary: No periodic closure or intersection uniqueness is inferred.
assumptions: The input is finite and contains enough distinct points for splprep.
The object exposes tck, u, verts, and interpolate.

inputs.name: vertices
inputs.constraints: Finite ordered points sufficient for the default quadratic splprep fit (at least three distinct points).

outputs.name: boundary
outputs.constraints: Stored verts have (200,2); interpolation returns coordinate arrays

preconditions: The input is finite and contains enough distinct points for splprep.
supported: Named finite boundary interpolation and endpoint behavior.
excluded: Polygon interior tests, crossing selection, and uniqueness guarantees.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Underlying array or SciPy spline validation errors propagate for unsupported vertices.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; fitting is a direct spline construction.
failure_semantics.partial_results: A failed constructor returns no boundary object.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel retains the documented scientific relation and implementation; applicable source-license obligations are recorded in licenses/Pleiades-MIT.txt.
provenance.license_status: Pleiades-derived source portions retain the MIT notice in licenses/Pleiades-MIT.txt; SciRel has no separate distribution-license declaration.

example.description: Fit a nonperiodic boundary spline to four ordered vertices.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry.fieldline import Boundary
b=Boundary(np.array([[0.,0.],[.3,.3],[.7,.7],[1.,1.]]))
assert b.verts.shape==(200,2)
example.expected: The boundary stores 200 fitted vertices with shape (200,2).

scope: Only the explicitly stated finite input domain and direct-test fixtures
verification.evidence_ceiling: Author numerical evidence for named fixtures, not arbitrary-input correctness, experimental physical validation, D2 completion, human approval or release.
known_limitations: No reliable intersection, polygon interior or uniqueness guarantee
